items.prompt:
Combining several media sources into one understanding is to:
A) integrate them
B) ignore them
C) delete them

How trustworthy a source is is its:
A) credibility
B) length
C) font

A chart presents information:
A) quantitatively/visually
B) only in sound
C) only as a story

You have a data chart, a news video, and an article on one issue. To INTEGRATE them means to:
A) combine what each contributes into one fuller understanding
B) use only the chart
C) ignore the article
items.answer: A) combine what each contributes into one fuller understanding

solution.answer: A) combine what each contributes into one fuller understanding

items.prompt:
To judge a source's CREDIBILITY, check:
A) the author's expertise, the organization, and whether it's accurate and current
B) its color
C) its word count only
items.answer: A) the author's expertise, the organization, and whether it's accurate and current

solution.answer: A) the author's expertise, the organization, and whether it's accurate and current

items.prompt:
Two sources on the same topic conflict. You should:
A) weigh their credibility and consult more reliable sources
B) believe the longer one
C) ignore the topic
items.answer: A) weigh their credibility and consult more reliable sources

solution.answer: A) weigh their credibility and consult more reliable sources

items.prompt:
An anonymous blog's statistic contradicts a government agency's report. The MORE credible source is:
A) the government agency's report
B) the anonymous blog
C) impossible to judge

The main benefit of INTEGRATING multiple media sources is to:
A) build a fuller, more accurate understanding than any one source gives
B) make the work longer
C) avoid judging sources
items.answer: A) build a fuller, more accurate understanding than any one source gives

solution.answer: A) build a fuller, more accurate understanding than any one source gives
